help.intro: A phone call of about one and a half minutes: Elif invites her friend Ben to her birthday party and they sort out the when, the where, the present and who picks up whom. On the way you learn two German birthday rules that surprise foreigners: you never congratulate before the day, and the birthday person brings the cake to work, not the colleagues. The scene is invented; the customs are real. You hear what you have just learnt: the accusative pronouns (Ich lade dich ein. Holst du mich ab? Ich kenne sie nicht) and separable verbs in a sentence (einladen, abholen, mitbringen, anrufen, anfangen: Ich hole dich um sieben ab). Listen once for the whole call, then once for the times and the tasks.
help.tips[0].text: The accusative pronouns are the object of the verb: Ich lade dich ein (I invite you). Holst du mich ab? (Do you pick me up?). Ich kenne ihn nicht (I do not know him). Wir sehen euch am Samstag (we see you all). Kennst du sie? (her / them). ich → mich, du → dich, er → ihn, wir → uns, ihr → euch change their form; sie, es and Sie stay the same.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: I invite you to my party. Can you pick me up at seven?
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Do you know Jonas? No, I do not know him. But I know her, his sister.
help.tips[0].check.why: anrufen takes the accusative: ich rufe dich an.
help.tips[1].title: Separable verbs in the sentence
help.tips[1].text: einladen, abholen, mitbringen, anrufen, anfangen, aufräumen: in a normal sentence the prefix goes to the end: Ich lade dich ein. Ich hole dich ab. Die Party fängt um acht an. Bring einen Salat mit! With a modal verb the whole verb stays together at the end: Kannst du mich abholen? Ich muss noch aufräumen. The stress is always on the prefix: EINladen, ABholen.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The party starts at eight. I pick you up at half past seven.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Can you bring a salad? I still have to tidy up.
help.tips[1].check.why: anfangen is separable and has a vowel change: die Party fängt … an.
help.remember[0]: Ich lade dich ein, du holst mich ab, ich kenne ihn nicht: mich, dich, ihn, uns, euch change; sie, es, Sie stay.
help.remember[1]: Separable verbs: prefix at the end (Ich hole dich ab), together after a modal (Kannst du mich abholen?).
help.exam: Short phone calls with invitations, times and arrangements are a typical listening task at this level.
help.hook: A birthday invitation, a cake rule nobody told you, and the question who picks up whom at half past six. Listen in.
passageTranslation:
Elif: Hello Ben, it is Elif!
Ben: Hello Elif! How are you?
Elif: Good! It is my birthday on Saturday and I am having a party. I invite you. Are you coming?
Ben: Of course I am coming! Happy birthday!
Elif: No, no, not yet! In Germany you do not congratulate before the birthday. It brings bad luck. Congratulate me on Saturday.
Ben: Oh, okay. Then I will congratulate you on Saturday. When does the party start?
Elif: At eight o'clock, at my place. Could you perhaps pick me up beforehand? I am picking up the cake at the bakery, and it is very big.
Ben: Sure. I will pick you up at half past six. Where is the bakery?
Elif: In Gartenstraße, next to the post office. I will call you on Saturday at six.
Ben: Good. Should I bring something?
Elif: Yes, please bring a salad. And music! You have good music.
Ben: Will do. And a present?
Elif: You do not have to buy anything. But if you want: I like reading. A book is great.
Ben: Is Jonas coming too?
Elif: Yes, I am inviting him too. And his sister. Do you know her?
Ben: No, I do not know her. But that is okay.
Elif: Oh, and one more thing: on Monday I am bringing a cake to the office for my colleagues. In Germany the person who has the birthday does that. Not the colleagues! So I am baking on Sunday.
Ben: Two cakes in one week. You are a lucky one. See you Saturday, Elif!
Elif: See you Saturday! And do not forget the salad!
